result:
V1 Fail-open
- `tls.rs::tls_from_vars`: any non-empty value among CERT/KEY/CA forces the all-three-required path; partial sets and SERVER_NAME-alone return `Err` before any file read, so no partial set can silently downgrade. Empty/whitespace-only values are folded into "unset" (`setting` closure trims); all-empty ⇒ `Ok(None)` ⇒ plain connect — this is the documented opt-in contract, not a silent fallback, since the operator set nothing that requests TLS.
- The one real gap: nothing validates the scheme/TLS pairing. `worker.rs` (rust/worker/src/bin/worker.rs:~55-64) and both spike bins (`driver.rs`, `worker.rs`) pass `tls_from_env()` output via `maybe_tls_options` to whatever `Url` came from `PG_TEMPORAL_ADDR`/`SPIKE_ADDR`. An operator who sets the three PEM vars but points at `http://...` (e.g. the spike default `http://127.0.0.1:7233`) gets TLS options handed to a cleartext endpoint; the safety of that combination depends entirely on the SDK rejecting it — it is not enforced in this code. `rust/TLS.md` documents "must be https" but no test or code checks it. Fail-open therefore hinges on unverified SDK behavior; a scheme check when `tls.is_some()` would close it deterministically.
- No combination yields "TLS with verification disabled": TlsOptions is only ever built with a CA-provided root (see V3), and there is no skip-verify flag touched.

V2 Secret handling
- `tls.rs::read_pem` constructs errors from `{var}`, `{path}` and `{e}` (io::Error Display). io::Error Display carries OS error text (ENOENT/EACCES), not file bytes; content is only returned on the success path and handed to the SDK. No `println!`/`log`/`Debug` of the PEM buffers anywhere in the diff; `ConnectionOptions` is built and passed to `Connection::connect`, never formatted.
- `tls_from_vars` error strings contain only variable names/paths. The binaries wrap the `String` error with `anyhow::anyhow!` — still just the path text. Clean.
- Minor latent note (not a diff defect): `ClientTlsOptions` fields are read in tests via direct field access, which suggests Debug may exist on SDK types; if any future code Debug-prints `ConnectionOptions`, key bytes as `Vec<u8>` would leak. Nothing in this change does so.

V3 Server verification
- `tls_from_vars` sets `server_root_ca_cert` from the CA file and `domain` from SERVER_NAME; no `accept_insecure`-style flag is used or available in the constructed options. `full_set_builds_tls_options` asserts the CA bytes and domain actually land in `TlsOptions`, so "CA given ⇒ custom root" is pinned at the unit level.
- Test-evidence gap: the `openssl s_server -Verify 1` check in `tls-handshake-check.sh` proves client-cert presentation but does not independently prove server-side verification (its server cert is trusted via the same CA the client loads; a wrong-CA/mismatched-SAN negative case isn't run). "No accidental system-roots-only when CA given" is asserted by construction, not verified end-to-end.

V4 Error paths
- `tls_from_vars`/`read_pem` use no `unwrap`/`panic`; every env-driven failure returns `Result::Err`. The `let (Some(..), Some(..), Some(..)) else { Err }` block is a defensive dead branch (comment acknowledges it) — unreachable, not a panic.
- Paths are trimmed before use (`setting`), so leading/trailing whitespace from env can't produce a spurious "file not found". Relative paths work (test `cert_alone_is_refused` relies on this). Non-PEM/garbage/binary files are read as bytes and passed to the SDK: no local panic, failure surfaces at connect as a TLS error — acceptable, though startup doesn't pre-validate PEM format.
- Binaries propagate `Url::from_str`/`Connection::connect` errors with `?`; no unwraps introduced. Test-only unwraps (`write`, `tempdir`) are dev code.

V5 Wiring
- Wired: `rust/worker/src/bin/worker.rs::main` (single `Connection::connect` in shown code), `rust/spikes/temporal-spike/src/bin/driver.rs::main`, `rust/spikes/temporal-spike/src/bin/worker.rs::main`. `lib.rs` in both crates export `pub mod tls`. No second connect path appears in the diff; the worker bin's pre-existing `let addr = ...` block above the connect is untouched and feeds the same options builder.
- Verification limits: the diff only proves there's no *other* connect in the changed hunks. Full-repo grep for `Connection::connect` (not possible from the material) should confirm no additional call sites exist in either crate.

V6 Test quality
- Refusal rules are genuinely pinned: `cert_alone_is_refused`, `cert_and_key_without_ca_is_refused` assert `missing` plus the absent var names and use nonexistent paths, proving refusal precedes file reads; `server_name_alone_is_refused` asserts all three var names; `empty_values_count_as_unset` pins trim-to-unset; `missing_file_names_var_and_path` pins error content. No `unwrap`-only vacuous asserts.
- Weak spots: (a) `assert!(!err.contains("PRIVATE KEY"))` in `missing_file_names_var_and_path` is a near-vacuous negative (contents can't reach that string by construction); (b) the full-set test passes fake PEM bytes, so SDK parsing/verification correctness is untested at unit level (hence the shell check); (c) no test asserts "TLS options ⇒ address must be https" because that rule isn't implemented; (d) shell check's "refused" case is refused by the server for a missing client cert, not by the client for the http/https mismatch.

GAMING: no - checked every assertion in tls.rs tests for vacuous or production-branch-bypassing asserts, one weak negative assert noted, no test-only code path found: 0 hits
VERDICT: fix - V1 medium: add an explicit scheme check rejecting https-required/TLS-vars vs http:// address in tls_from_env callers (or helper) rather than relying on unverified SDK behavior; low: prove server verification in the shell check with a wrong-CA/SAN negative; nit: drop or strengthen the near-vacuous PRIVATE KEY assert
